preamble: In many Japanese dialects, including Standard Japanese (traditionally), the voiced velar plosive [g] is realized as a velar nasal [ŋ] when it occurs in intervocalic positions or word-medially.

examples.note: Bidakuon (鼻濁音): for consistent nasal speakers, word-internal /ɡ/ in native morphemes is realized as [ŋ]; word-initially all speakers use [ɡ].

sources: Ladefoged, P., & Maddieson, I. (1996). The Sounds of the World's Languages. Blackwell. https://www.wiley.com/en-us/The+Sounds+of+the+World%27s+Languages-p-9780631198154
